name: Meola Reef Reserve
access: Meola Rd, Point Chevalier; park at the reserve entrance.
best: Reef and harbour-edge flying with the city skyline behind you; shallow water at low tide.
hazards: Dog walkers early and late, motorway noise, mudflats at low tide, harbour traffic.
note: A dog park on the point — fine for a quick session, not a destination.

name: Eric Armishaw Park
access: Eric Armishaw Park, off Great North Rd, Waterview.
best: Quiet harbour-side reserve with open grass and a long water line toward the bridge.
hazards: Shared-path cyclists, dog walkers, tidal mud.
note: Overshadowed by Point Chevalier but emptier and easier to park.

name: Western Springs Park
access: Great North Rd or Motions Rd; park at the stadium end.
best: Big open lawns and a lake — good for tuning and low-altitude practice, not scenery.
hazards: Very busy paths, geese, sports events, motorway on the boundary.
note: A test-and-tune field. Don't expect solitude.

name: Keith Hay Park
access: Keith Hay Park, off Hillsborough Rd, Mount Roskill.
best: Large flat sports fields with room for gate practice and long sightlines.
hazards: Sports fields in use most evenings and weekends, netball crowds.
note: Useful when Fearon Park is busy — same area, more space.

name: Cockle Bay Beach
access: Cockle Bay Beach, off Shelly Beach Parade, Howick.
best: Sheltered bay with a small beach, rocks and a jetty — calm water in most winds.
hazards: Swimmers and kayakers in summer, moored boats, shellfish beds at low tide.
note: Better in an easterly than the bigger Howick beaches.

name: Shelly Park Beach
access: Shelly Park Beach, end of Sandspit Rd.
best: Mangrove estuary and sand flats — flat water, big skies, very few people.
hazards: Mud and mangroves at low tide, shorebirds Sep-Mar, no shade.
note: Pairs with Mangemangeroa next door; fly the estuary on a rising tide.

name: Mellons Bay Beach
access: Mellons Bay Beach, off Bleakhouse Rd, Howick.
best: Pohutukawa-backed beach with cliffs at the southern end and Rangitoto on the horizon.
hazards: Cliff updraughts, swimmers in summer, narrow beach at high tide.
note: Quieter than Howick Beach and a better shoreline for low passes.

name: Howick Beach
access: Howick Beach, off Granger Rd; car park at the end.
best: Long sandy beach, jetty and the Howick village edge — easy access for a quick flight.
hazards: Busy in summer, jetty users, moored boats.
note: Convenience spot — the beach is the draw, the crowds are the cost.

name: Macleans Park
access: Macleans Park, off Macleans Rd, Bucklands Beach.
best: Big sports fields with bush edges — good for tuning and short-range practice.
hazards: School and club sport, cricket nets, dog walkers.
note: A practical field rather than a scenic spot.

name: Umupuia Beach
access: Umupuia Beach, off Maraetai Coast Rd; gravel car park at the end.
best: Wide tidal estuary, sand flats and farmland — empty most days, huge open lines.
hazards: Tidal flats cut you off, soft sand, stock nearby, patchy phone coverage.
note: One of the quietest beaches inside the Auckland boundary.

name: Duder Regional Park
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Duder Regional Park, off North Rd, Maraetai; gate at the end of the road.
best: Coastal farmland, cliffs and empty beaches — the best scenery on the Pohutukawa Coast.
hazards: Stock, cliff edges, permit conditions, no water or shelter.
note: Needs an Auckland Council regional park permit — worth it for the cliff lines.

name: Narrow Neck Beach
access: Narrow Neck Beach, off Old Lake Rd, Devonport.
best: Long east-facing beach with the harbour and Rangitoto in frame; sheltered in a westerly.
hazards: Swimmers, paddleboarders, ferry wakes, cliff at the north end.
note: The best Devonport beach that still sits outside the harbour control zone.

name: Little Manly Beach
access: Little Manly Beach, off Ngaio St, Manly.
best: Small sheltered bay with rocks and a wharf — flat water in most conditions.
hazards: Wharf users, moored boats, ferry traffic from Gulf Harbour.
note: Shelter when the east-coast beaches are blown out.

name: Matakatia Bay
access: Matakatia Beach, off Matakatia Pde.
best: Quiet residential bay with a long low-tide sandbar and clear water.
hazards: Residents' moorings, low-tide mud, narrow launch at high tide.
note: A locals-only feel; keep the noise down and stay off the sandbar at low tide.

name: Arkles Bay Beach
access: Arkles Bay Beach, off Arkles Strand.
best: Sheltered swimming beach with a boat ramp and a rocky point at the north end.
hazards: Boat ramp traffic in summer, swimmers, kayaks.
note: The ramp makes carrying gear easy; the same ramp makes it busy on a Saturday morning.

name: Army Bay
access: Army Bay, end of Whangaparaoa Rd; car park by the beach.
best: Wide bay with a long beach, rocky ends and open water toward Tiritiri Matangi.
hazards: Boat traffic to Gulf Harbour, divers in summer, wind funnelling down the peninsula.
note: The pick of the Whangaparaoa bays for open-water lines.

name: Shakespear Regional Park
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Shakespear Regional Park, end of Whangaparaoa Rd; gate opens 6am.
best: Cliffs, farmland and three bays — the most varied flying on the peninsula.
hazards: Stock, cliff updraughts, heavy weekend visitation, permit conditions.
note: Needs a regional park permit; the northern cliffs are the reason to bother.

name: Scandrett Regional Park
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Scandrett Regional Park, off Scandrett Rd, Mahurangi East.
best: Rolling coastal farmland above the Mahurangi harbour — huge sightlines, nobody around.
hazards: Stock, steep drops to the water, gravel road in, permit conditions.
note: The quietest regional park in the north; pair it with a Mahurangi West trip.

name: Ti Point
access: Ti Point Rd, off Leigh Rd; small reserve at the end.
best: Rocky coast and bush at the mouth of the Matakana river — quiet and unusual.
hazards: Private land either side, rocky shore, tide.
note: Stay on the reserve — the surrounding blocks are private.

name: Te Arai Beach
access: Te Arai Point Rd, off Pakiri Rd; gravel car park at the point.
best: Long empty surf beach, dunes and forestry blocks — the wildest flying in the region.
hazards: Surf and rips, no patrols, forestry operations, soft sand, no phone coverage.
note: An hour and a half from the city and worth every minute of it.

name: Ceramco Park
access: Ceramco Park, off Great North Rd, Glendene.
best: Big flat fields and a stream — tuning and practice, not scenery.
hazards: Rugby and league fixtures, dog walkers, stream at the boundary.
note: West Auckland's equivalent of Lloyd Elsmore — a field, not a destination.

name: Wattle Bay
access: Wattle Bay Rd, Laingholm; park at the reserve at the end.
best: Tiny bush-ringed cove on the Manukau — sheltered, green water, almost nobody.
hazards: Steep bush tracks, mud at low tide, no phone coverage.
note: One of the few Waitakere-side bays you can legally fly — it sits outside the ranges park.

name: Ararimu
access: Ararimu Rd, off Paparimu Rd; park on the verge and don't block gates.
best: Rolling farmland and shelterbelts with long open lines in every direction.
hazards: Private land, stock, farm machinery, narrow roads.
note: Ask the landowner before launching — the whole valley is private farmland.

name: Pollok
access: Pollok Rd, off Awhitu Rd; verge parking only.
best: Hill country above the Manukau with big views and no people.
hazards: Private farmland, stock, gravel roads, wind.
note: Permission needed — this is working farmland, not reserve.

name: Ramarama
access: Ramarama Rd, off State Highway 1; park at the hall.
best: Market gardens and open flats with the Bombay hills behind.
hazards: Greenhouses and polythene, orchard netting, highway traffic, private land.
note: Greenhouse country — watch for netting and stay off the crops.

name: Paerata
access: Paerata Rd, off Great South Rd.
best: Open farmland with the Drury hills and the harbour beyond.
hazards: Earthworks and new subdivisions, highway, private land.
note: Changing fast with the Drury development — check the ground before you go.

name: Mauku
access: Mauku Rd, off Glenbrook Rd; park at the hall.
best: Quiet dairy country with drains, hedgerows and long flat lines.
hazards: Stock, drains, private land, milk tankers on the road.
note: Ask first — the paddocks are all in production.

name: Kohekohe
access: Kohekohe Rd, off Awhitu Rd; verge parking.
best: Deep rural Awhitu — hills, bush remnants and nobody for kilometres.
hazards: Private land, stock, gravel, no phone coverage.
note: The most remote spot on the Awhitu road; permission essential.

name: Patumahoe
access: Patumahoe Rd; park at the domain.
best: Village domain and surrounding farmland — easy access, open skies.
hazards: Village traffic, private paddocks, sport on the domain.
note: Launch from the domain and fly the edges; ask before crossing into paddocks.

name: Puni
access: Puni Rd, off Great South Rd.
best: Flat farmland on the Puni flats — open airspace and nothing to hit.
hazards: Private land, stock, State Highway 1 nearby.
note: Simple open-country flying; permission needed.
